Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 7:36 P.M.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Councilmember Macias

Invocation was given by Deacon Juan Garcia, Saint Frances of Rome Church

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
 ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo.

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Martinez, Chief of Police Bertelsen, Director of Economic and
Community Development Marquez, Director of Administrative Services Johnson, Director of Utilities Robledo, Director
of Community Resources Carpenter, Director of Public Works/City Engineer Delgadillo, Director of Information
Technology and Library Services Graf, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia, Planning Manager Munoz, and Chief
Deputy City Clerk Garcia.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

The City Council reconvened at 7:36 P.M.; City Attorney Martinez announced the following regarding Closed Session:
Item 1 and 2 - All members were present, No reportable action. Item 3 was not heard.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Joe Guerrera requested Council to appoint a member for representation in the Golden Days Committee. He added that
Azusa Golden Days will take place this year and details are still being discussed.
Ryan provided a statement on behalf of Hilda Solis in regards to the importance getting vaccine against Covid-19; he
added information on an approved motion from the LA County Board of Supervisors to ensure the provision of Social
Security benefits for the youth and foster care.

REPORTS, UPDATES AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez provided an update on Golden Days; Golden Days will take place October 2nd through October
9th, every event will take place except the carnival; due to uncertainty and risks the insurance company (JIPA)
recommended a carnival not take place; the carnival will be supplemented with other activities.
Director of Community Resources Carpenter added that the existing MOU with the Golden Days Committee is dated back
on 2005 and needs updates; most non- profits holding fundraiser will go virtual/ hybrid this year; JIPA has flagged the
carnival as a high risk event.
City Manager Gonzalez introduced newly assigned Acting Assistant Fire Chief, Carlos Flores to Azusa.

4th of July Recap

Chief Bertelsen provided a brief recap related to fourth of July activities, enforcement and operations in the city of Azusa;
for the period of July 2 through July 5 the Police Department had a total of 198 firework related calls, 128 of those calls
were on fourth of July; 5 small fires were report; 29 citations were issued; 32 citations issued on fourth of July; there were
3 repeat offenders; 3 juveniles were citied; approximately 1/3 of citations were given to non-Azusa residents; about 100
pounds of fireworks were seized and handed to the LA County Fire for proper disposal.

Speed Humps/Table Policy Discussion

Director of Public Works and City Engineer Delgadillo provided a brief presentation regarding a Speed Hump/Table
Policy. Speed bumps, speed humps and speed tables were options presented. Delgadillo requested council to provide
guidance as to move forward with a draft policy at a future meeting.
Delgadillo answered questions posed by the Council stating that Public Works and the Azusa Police Department work on
calming traffic solutions when incidents occur by reviewing incident records. Delgadillo added that installing speed
humps on streets with a limit of 35 mph or higher is not recommended, as it would be hazardous, discussion was held.

Council Comments

Mayor Pro Tem Avila extended his condolences to the family of Connie Cornejo Chavarria; Pastor Griffin from Azusa
Sandals Church put together a community event with One Day LA; 1,000 volunteers will be provided to assist with 20
different improvement projects throughout the city; reminded the community to mark their calendars for National Night
Out on Tuesday, August 3rd.

PAGE TWO – 7/19/2021
 Councilmember Macias requested a follow up from staff regarding freeway on ramp and off ramp signs; and excessive
trash in and around the Gold Line; Macias provided a short video with updates on Foothill Gold line extension to
Claremont.
Delgadillo answered questions posed by the Council stating request have been submitted to Caltrans regarding freeway
signage, response is pending; and efforts to clean up the Metro Gold Line are actively effect.
Councilmember Alvarez announced the Library will be hosting, Reading Colors your World Week which will take place
July19 – 23rd; the activities taking place are Summer Reading Virtual Bugs Safari for the family, Blast Off Live Stream
Stem Craft for kids and Crafts for older teens and adults. Prizes will also be raffled to kids registered; Alvarez asked staff
to survey the street light sensors.
Councilmember Mendez requested staff to look into two signal lights on Azusa Ave. by Target and 9th Street and
Pasadena Ave. stating the timing of the traffic lights are off which contributes to long wait times.
Director of Public Works and City Engineer Delgadillo responded to questions posed by Council stating the City of Azusa
does not have the authority to make any changes to the traffic lights by the Metro tracks; staff will reach out to Metro and
an update will be provided at a later date.
Mayor Gonzales congratulated the Community Resources Department on a job well done on organizing Drive-in Concerts
in the Park; National Night Out is an annual event and walk against crime, 20 agencies will be present and will be
highlighting the services that we provide for the community; on August 15th, the 12th Annual Kathy’s Cool Kutz will take
place, volunteers from local salons and barbershops will be providing kids with a free haircut and school supplies; thanked
and wished good luck to city staff, Sylvia and Annette on their new career endeavors.
SCHEDULED ITEMS – CITY COUNCIL

PUBLIC HEARING – 2021 REFUSE AND ORGANICS RATE ADJUSTMENT.

Environmental Programs Specialist Sagun presented the Staff Report stating that it is a contractual rate adjustment as part
of the City’s contract with Athens; due to Proposition 218 Right to Vote Act, it must be considered as a public hearing;
annual rate adjustments are allowed based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for the services provided and landfill
provider costs; rate increases are modes at $4.71 for single family, $1.29 for multi-family, and -$6.00 for commercial; and
rates are competitive when compared to other cities.

Mayor Gonzales declared the hearing open.

City Clerk Cornejo read the affidavit of proof of publication published on July9, 2021, in the San Gabriel Valley Tribune.
Three letters of opposition were received and provided to the Council.

Public Comment

None.

Moved by Councilmember Mendez, seconded by Mayor Pro-Tem Avila and carried by the unanimous vote of the Council
to close the public hearing.
